audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Exodus / Shemot text tradition, Song of the Sea poetic layer; draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Song of the Sea, Miriam, women with timbrels, Marah, healing statute/testing.

verses.restored: Then Moses and children of Israel sang this song to YHWH, and they said: I will sing to YHWH, for rising, he has risen; horse and rider he hurled into sea.

familiar.text: Then sang Moses and the children of Israel this song unto the LORD, and spake, saying, I will sing unto the LORD, for he hath triumphed gloriously: the horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea.

modern.text: Then Moses and the Israelites sang this song to the LORD: “I will sing to the LORD, for He is highly exalted. The horse and rider He has thrown into the sea.

original.text: אָ֣ז יָשִֽׁיר מֹשֶׁה֩ וּבְנֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל אֶת הַשִּׁירָ֤ה הַזֹּאת֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ לֵאמֹ֑ר אָשִׁ֤ירָה לַֽיהוָה֙ כִּֽי גָאֹ֣ה גָּאָ֔ה ס֥וּס וְרֹכְב֖וֹ רָמָ֥ה בַיָּֽם

verses.restored: Yah is my strength and song, and he became for me salvation/healing; this is my Divine, and I will beautify/praise him, Divine of my father, and I will exalt him.

modern.text: Pharaoh’s chariots and army He has cast into the sea; the finest of his officers are drowned in the Red Sea.

original.text: מַרְכְּבֹ֥ת פַּרְעֹ֛ה וְחֵיל֖וֹ יָרָ֣ה בַיָּ֑ם וּמִבְחַ֥ר שָֽׁלִשָׁ֖יו טֻבְּע֥וּ בְיַם סֽוּף

verses.restored: Deeps cover them; they went down into depths like stone.

familiar.text: The depths have covered them: they sank into the bottom as a stone.

modern.text: The depths have covered them; they sank there like a stone.

original.text: תְּהֹמֹ֖ת יְכַסְיֻ֑מוּ יָרְד֥וּ בִמְצוֹלֹ֖ת כְּמוֹ אָֽבֶן

verses.restored: Your right hand, YHWH, majestic in power; your right hand, YHWH, shatters enemy.

modern.text: Your right hand, O LORD, is majestic in power; Your right hand, O LORD, has shattered the enemy.

original.text: יְמִֽינְךָ֣ יְהוָ֔ה נֶאְדָּרִ֖י בַּכֹּ֑חַ יְמִֽינְךָ֥ יְהוָ֖ה תִּרְעַ֥ץ אוֹיֵֽב

verses.restored: In greatness of your majesty you tear down those rising against you; you send your burning anger; it consumes them like stubble.

familiar.text: And in the greatness of thine excellency thou hast overthrown them that rose up against thee: thou sentest forth thy wrath, which consumed them as stubble.

modern.text: You overthrew Your adversaries by Your great majesty. You unleashed Your burning wrath; it consumed them like stubble.

verses.restored: By breath/wind of your nostrils waters piled up; floods stood like heap; deeps congealed in heart of sea.

familiar.text: And with the blast of thy nostrils the waters were gathered together, the floods stood upright as an heap, and the depths were congealed in the heart of the sea.

modern.text: At the blast of Your nostrils the waters piled up; like a wall the currents stood firm; the depths congealed in the heart of the sea.

original.text: וּבְר֤וּחַ אַפֶּ֨יךָ֙ נֶ֣עֶרְמוּ מַ֔יִם נִצְּב֥וּ כְמוֹ נֵ֖ד נֹזְלִ֑ים קָֽפְא֥וּ תְהֹמֹ֖ת בְּלֶב יָֽם

modern.text: The enemy declared, ‘I will pursue, I will overtake. I will divide the spoils; I will gorge myself on them. I will draw my sword; my hand will destroy them.’

translation_notes: Song of the Sea is ancient victory poetry; preserve its intensity while not turning it into ethnic hatred.
Ruach/wind/breath imagery links sea deliverance to Divine power.
Miriam is explicitly prophetess and leads women with timbrels and dances; preserve her leadership.
Marah moves from victory song to wilderness thirst; YHWH as healer closes the chapter.
The tree/wood sweetening bitter waters should be preserved without over-allegorizing in the source layer.
safety_note: The victory song celebrates liberation from Pharaoh's chariot army, not hatred of Egyptians as a people. Violent poetic imagery should be read as ancient liberation hymn against oppressive military pursuit.
